caption: What if friction vanished for just 5 seconds? Friction is the grip between two surfaces, and almost everything depends on it. Walking works because your foot pushes the ground backwards and friction pushes you forward. Without it you'd just slip in place. A car tyre on clean, dry asphalt has a friction coefficient of about 0.7. At zero there are no brakes and no steering, so every auto just keeps sliding. Nails and screws stay put partly thanks to friction, knots need it to stay tied, and even spun yarn holds together because its fibres grip each other. And by Newton's first law, anything already moving keeps moving until something slows it down. Then friction returns, and everything skids to a stop in one big pile. What would YOU grab first? 👇
